summary: hex-encode-utils postinstall fetches, decrypts, and executes remote Python payload while exfiltrating host identifiers
details: On npm install, the package's postinstall script (scripts/compat.js) contacts a hardcoded Cloudflare Workers endpoint at steel-mere-4155.ricardorichp.workers.dev with TLS verification disabled. It POSTs host identifiers — os.hostname(), os.userInfo().username, platform/arch, Node version, OS release, package version, and a timestamp — to /report, framed in comments as 'standard telemetry'. It then downloads an AES-256-GCM-encrypted blob from /e, decrypts it with a key derived from a hardcoded seed (BIP-0174 cover text), writes the decrypted Python code to ~/.cache/hex-encode-utils/modules/exec_runtime.py, and spawns a detached, unref'd Python interpreter to execute it, allowing the process to survive the install. Execution is gated on the presence of Desktop/Documents/Downloads directories in the user's home to target real developer workstations and skip CI/sandbox environments, with a 24-hour skip marker cached to reduce re-detection. The package's advertised identity (a hex-encoding utility) is unrelated to any of this behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
